reason: Obtusely serrate teeth are still serrate. The degree word is lost, but the quality holds.
Virescent means becoming green or greenish, and green is the closest PATO term.
Curling backward is recurved.
Pellicular means thin and skin-like, which is membranous. I did not find the label of FLOPO_0991046 in the value-term file, so this rests on the rule's stated label.
Radicating means rooting, usually at nodes. That is shoot-borne roots present, and PO_0000042 lists adventitious root as a synonym.
French cannelée means channelled, fluted or grooved, which is furrowed.
Nervured means veined, and PO_0005020 lists vein as a synonym.
Non-peltate is the negation of peltate. FLOPO_0991107 is peltate under attachment quality.
Piano-convex is a spelling variant of plano-convex.
Hirtous means shaggy with stiff hairs, which is hirsute. The label of FLOPO_0991050 was not checked in the file.
Pungent-apiculate means a short tip that is also stiff and sharp. Mucronate is an abrupt small point and loses the pungency. A spine-tipped or apiculate mapping would also be partial.
A fringe of hairs is a fringed margin, as in ciliate.
Without a significant palea means the palea is absent or vestigial. The rule treats it as absent. The word 'significant' makes this a mild stretch.
Brick-shaped is rectangular.
Pungent can mean sharp-pointed or acrid in taste and smell. 'Not sharp' is right only for pointed parts, not for odour or taste.
Collapsing is collapsed. The wording is a process, but descriptions use it as a state.
Broadly ellipsoidal is elliptic. The degree of breadth is lost, but the shape holds.
Doubly serrulate (biserrulate) means small teeth that carry still smaller teeth. Plain serrulate loses the double toothing.
Tattering means the margin is irregularly torn, which is lacerate.
Incised-serrate means cut and toothed. Serrated keeps the teeth but loses the incision.
Without vittae means no oil tubes, as in Apiaceae fruits, so vitta absent. The FLOPO_0986042 id was not looked up.
Piriform means pear-shaped.
Hypocrateriform is the same as salverform. The word in the rule is a misspelling.
French incliné means inclined or slanting, which is an oblique orientation. It could also mean ascending or leaning.
French saillante means projecting, which is prominent.
Sarcotestal means the seed has a fleshy seed coat. 'Fleshy' belongs on the testa or seed coat only.
Tufted-pilose means hairs gathered in tufts, which is close to bearded (long hairs confined to a tuft). The pilose part is lost.
The prominence belongs to the nerves, not to the part. Prominent on the leaf would be wrong. The right form is vein with prominent, or a prominent-veined value.
Spinetipped is spine-tipped, written as one word.
Glandular-puncticulate means finely dotted with glands, which is gland-dotted.
Insipid means tasteless.
Pappose means having a pappus.
Ill-scented is foetid, which is an unpleasant odour.
Lamelliform means shaped like a plate or lamella.
Glandular-hairless is ambiguous. It may mean glandular and without hairs, or without glandular hairs. Rejected rather than mapped to glandular trichome absent.
Reticulate veined is reticulate venation.
Aristiform means awn- or bristle-like, which is close to setaceous.
Beak-shaped is close to beaked. It means shaped like a beak, while beaked means having a beak.
Comblike is pectinate.
Mallet-shaped means a head that is abruptly thicker than its stalk, which is close to clavate.
Without crest is not crested.
Ecalcarate means without a spur. The target is the corolla spur, so it is wrong for a spur on the calyx or sepals.
Incanous means hoary, with grey-white hairs, which is canescent.
Spathate means having a spathe, and PO_0009054 lists spathe as a synonym.
Not bearded is the negation of bearded.
Short-caulescent means a short stem. 'Stem present' loses the shortness, which is the point of the word.
Squamiform means scale-shaped.
Densely inserted means crowded.
Gymnostomous mosses have a capsule without a peristome.
Weakly thickened is thickened. The degree word is lost, but the quality holds.
